3f221819b7e801230c0fd7707fd84fd7404e0299: Cambre d'Aze is a small, low-key resort: 22 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where you come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts. Cambre d'Aze's family reputation is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Pyrenees for getting children started on skiing. The altitude of Cambre d'Aze (1700 m at the bottom, 2408 m at the top) helps it keep decent snow through mid-winter. January and February are the most reliable months; in December and March, it is wise to check conditions before finalising a booking. At €40, the day pass places Cambre d'Aze among the mid-range resorts on budget: neither cheap nor exorbitant. The quality of the ski area and facilities justifies the price for most skiers. In short, Cambre d'Aze doesn't compete with the giants of skiing and doesn't pretend to. It's an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.
3f22a2e03b23e38817caaff141e4f2960c9843ce: La Grave - La Meije is a small, low-key resort, with 2 km of runs offering an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where you come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts. The terrain is the main draw at La Grave - La Meije: with 0 black and 0 red runs on offer, confident skiers will find plenty to challenge them. Off-piste and freeride are practised here, often in excellent conditions thanks to the altitude and the orientation of the slopes. As for snow reliability, La Grave - La Meije is in a strong position: with its summit at 3,568 m, even in difficult winters the upper runs hold up well into April. The village at 1,450 m is also well placed to offer comfortable conditions from mid-December. The budget for a stay at La Grave - La Meije is clearly high: €66 for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence, but you need to be aware of it before you set off. In short: La Grave - La Meije does not rival the giants of skiing and does not pretend to. It is an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.
